text: Nghe An rolls out 2027 trade promotion plan to boost market access

The People's Committee of central Nghe An Province has issued Plan No. 1038/KH-UBND on trade promotion for 2027, aiming to strengthen supply-demand connections, expand domestic consumption markets, and boost exports.
Under the plan, Nghe An will focus promotional resources on competitive product groups, key staples, and items with strong market development potential.

Priority sectors include processed agricultural, forestry, and aquatic products; food and beverages; One Commune One Product (OCOP) items; outstanding rural industrial products; handicrafts and textiles; as well as several advantageous industrial goods.
A key target is to organize or support at least 20 domestic trade promotion, export promotion, and e-commerce activities in 2027.

Through these initiatives, the province aims to assist at least 250 businesses, cooperatives, household businesses, and production entities in participating in promotional programs, with priority given to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), cooperatives, and OCOP producers.

For the domestic market, the locality aims to organize or support local businesses in joining at least 10 trade fairs, exhibitions, product weeks, showcase events, and supply-demand matching programs.
These activities will be held locally as well as in major consumer hubs such as Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, and other high-potential markets.
Through these events, local enterprises will gain greater access to distribution networks, retailers, procurement companies, and consumption partners.
This strategy directly addresses a common bottleneck among small-scale producers: possessing competitive products but lacking access to major distribution channels and broader markets.
On the export front, the province plans to organize or participate in three to five trade missions, market surveys, fairs, or exhibitions to drive outbound shipments.
Notably, at least one of these activities must target the Halal market or emerging markets.

Alongside expanding export destinations, Nghe An plans to strengthen coordination with the Vietnam Trade Promotion Agency (VIETRADE) under the Ministry of Industry and Trade, Vietnam's overseas trade offices, diplomatic missions, industry associations, and trade promotion organizations to provide market intelligence, introduce partners, and help local businesses connect with foreign importers.
Additionally, the province has identified e-commerce and digital transformation as key tools for market expansion.

Under the plan, the province strives to provide training and consulting for at least 100 businesses, cooperatives, and producers on e-commerce, digital transformation, trade negotiation skills, rules of origin, market standards, and brand development.

Participating enterprises and cooperatives will receive support to build and standardize digital storefronts, product descriptions, photos, videos, QR codes, and traceability data, alongside payment and logistics solutions on suitable e-commerce platforms.
Nghe An's OCOP products are increasingly refined in both quality and design.

In parallel, Nghe An Province will focus on building and updating a centralized database covering local enterprises, cooperatives, OCOP items, outstanding rural industrial products, key staples, and goods with strong export potential.
